name: Aries
introduction: is the Ram whose golden fleece Jason and the Argonauts set out to find. It is a small zodiac constellation, marked mainly by a short, bent line of three stars between Pisces and Taurus, best seen on northern autumn and winter evenings.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Some 2,000 years ago, the Sun crossed the celestial equator heading north, at the March equinox, while it was in Aries. Astronomers still call that point the First Point of Aries, even though Earth’s slowly wobbling axis has since moved the equinox into Pisces.

Aries also contains one of our nearest neighbors. [Teegarden’s Star](id:10pc-0056), a faint red dwarf about 12.5 light-years away, was discovered only in 2003. It has at least two Earth-mass planets, one of which receives about as much light from its star as Earth does from the Sun.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Hamal](hip:9884), the brightest star, is an orange giant 66 light-years away, orbited by a giant planet. [Sheratan](hip:8903) is a white star 59 light-years away.

[Mesarthim](hip:8832) is a lovely pair of white stars of nearly equal brightness. In 1664, Robert Hooke noticed that it was double while following a comet, making it one of the first double stars discovered with a telescope. [Bharani](hip:13209) marks the ram’s tail.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: Aries looks away from the Milky Way, toward distant galaxies such as the large spiral NGC 772. In June, the Daytime Arietid meteor shower radiates from Aries; it is one of the strongest of the year, but its meteors arrive mainly in daylight.
